reason: E3 directly supports heterogeneous lattice strain causing unusual dislocation behaviors (kinks, cross-slips) and strengthening, and E1 supports low average SFE with possible local variation modulating dislocation behavior and nanoscale crack bridging. However, no cited evidence directly supports the causal link that raising average SFE and reducing its variability suppresses these mechanisms and reduces toughness, nor that a minor additive achieves this SFE change.
premises: Local SFE heterogeneity exists in single-phase FCC HEAs due to random elemental mixing
SFE heterogeneity enables multiple non-conventional dislocation processes (nano-twinning, kinks, cross-slip)
These dislocation processes bridge cracks and delay failure, retaining toughness
A minor additive that raises average SFE and reduces its variability will suppress these processes
Suppressing these processes will measurably reduce fracture toughness
